changes_since_r46: P0 defect fix: '[object Object]' in the deployed supplier draft. Root cause traced precisely -- _build_response_draft() has always returned a structured {subject, body, status} object by design (matching the generic commercial_answer renderer's own correct handling); the R46 wiring fix's renderSupplierRequestAnswer coerced the whole object to a string instead of extracting .subject/.body. Fixed by extracting the fields, matching the pattern already proven correct elsewhere -- not a frontend workaround.

next_move genericity fix: two of three next_move items were gated on conditions true for virtually every price_increase case, so they appeared identically across materially different situations, including nonsensical combinations (requesting supplier evidence on a case that was just accepted). Now gated on the actual decision state -- a genuinely pending alternative-supplier qualification (reusing the same signal trade_off already reflects) and the actual decision stance.

Decision-stance classifier precision fix: a plain substring check for 'accept' incorrectly matched 'before accepting the 8%' and would have matched 'do not accept'. Fixed by checking negated/conditional forms first.

Stance-aware next_move fallback: previously one generic sentence regardless of decision; now distinct fallback text for accept/investigate/challenge, closing a gap where accept and investigate cases could collapse to an identical next_move.

Supplier draft situation-tailoring: investigated whether a structured decision-type field already exists (found DecisionType -- optimization/constraint_satisfaction, a different axis; no field distinguishes timing/FX/contract-index/competition situations). Built _classify_situation_type() layered on the existing stance classifier, using a real structured signal (a genuine alternative supplier present in case evidence) where one exists. Eight situation-specific draft templates (accept, challenge, investigate-suppressed, contract_compliance, timing, fx, competition, strategic_continuity) replace the single generic template, each using only facts the case actually states.

known_limitations: No live Anthropic API key exists anywhere in this build or the environment that produced it. Live model behavior remains completely unverified for Supplier Request, as for every other experience. tests/live_certification_harness.py is ready to run the moment a real key is available.

No browser automation tool is available in this environment. Deployment validation used a genuine running server process and real HTTP requests, confirmed to differ meaningfully from the in-process TestClient, but true browser rendering, console errors, and visual layout have never been observed.

The 8-situation supplier-draft classifier (_classify_situation_type) is deterministic text-pattern matching layered on structured signals where they exist, not a fully structured model-output field -- documented honestly in the code as a smaller, safer choice than extending the live classifier's JSON contract, which would be untestable without a real API key.

Money materiality (whether a small routine adjustment should suppress the Money section) was investigated properly this pass and deliberately left as-is, with reasoning recorded: every alternative considered either required an arbitrary dollar threshold or hid legitimate budget information.

The generic usefulness-scoring/composition engine remains deliberately unbuilt across every experience -- no finding in any Supplier Request certification round has shown the current adaptive-composition architecture structurally incapable of the required behavior.
